decisions.issues: Clean. Matches the beat: dusk hill under mango trees, a low two-tiered tiled gateway near the crown, the stone stair, a small party of torch-bearing Nair guards and horses with nobody readable as a rider, no banners or palanquin, no painted text. The open dusk sky across the upper left and centre gives plenty of room for both captions.

Acceptable with minor misses. Varma's knot sits high at the back of the crown rather than clearly above his LEFT ear. The sandal-paste line on his brow is not visible. His seat on the horse is a little ambiguous because the mundu hides his leg. Ramayyan wears a tiny ear stud that his sheet does not show. Everything else holds: Varma is bare-headed with no crest or spear, wears pearl drop earrings and one gold chain, and has a cream mundu with a gold border. Ramayyan has his receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, and looks up at the king. No text. The dusk sky at the upper centre-left holds both balloons.

Varma does not match his sheet. His hair is a loose curly mane with no side knot above the LEFT ear, he wears round gold ball earrings instead of pearl drops, and his rounder face reads as Nagoji's sheet (curly hair, gold drop earring). With the real Nagoji standing in the same panel, readers could mix the two up. Nagoji's Goa brand is drawn as a dark inked tattoo-like sigil on top of the forearm. That reads as a symbol or pseudo-glyph, close to a cross, when it should be a pale puckered scar patch on the inner left forearm. Varma is still seated, not clearly dismounting. The heir sits on the horse's neck in front of the saddle. Nagoji's shoulder cloth has a wide gold border where the script asks for plain cream.
decisions.correction: Varma must not resemble Nagoji. Draw his face exactly from the varma-v1 sheet's profile study: a long, lean face with high cheekbones, a long straight nose and deep-set eyes. Comb his black hair smooth and tie it in one compact knot above and behind his LEFT ear, with no loose curls falling to the shoulders. Give him WHITE PEARL drop earrings (never gold balls), one gold chain, a thin line of sandal paste across the brow and a cream mundu with a thin gold border. Show him actually dismounting: one leg swung over the saddle and a bare foot reaching for the red earth. He passes the reins down to the turbaned stable boy while his eyes stay ahead, not on the boy. The heir (about ten, small white mundu, thin gold chain, small topknot) stays mounted in the saddle of a second horse just behind him, not on a horse's neck. Nagoji on the right keeps his high topknot, grey temples, tiny flush gold stud, thick curled moustache, clean chin and silver chain, with a PLAIN cream shoulder cloth (no wide gold border) so he never matches the king. His old brand is only a pale, flesh-toned, puckered patch of raised scar ridges on the INNER left forearm beside the long thin white scar: never a dark inked mark, tattoo, symbol, letter or cross. Better still, turn that forearm inward so the brand is barely seen. Keep the torchlit hill, the stair rising to the lit gateway, the background guards and the open dusk sky at upper left for the balloon.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The sandal-paste line on Varma's brow is not visible, and he has a cream cloth over one shoulder (still bare-chested, not forbidden). Otherwise strong: Varma's profile matches the varma-v1 face study, with hair tied in a knot behind the left ear, a pearl drop earring, one gold chain, no crest and no spear. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus) and faces the king closely. The Nair guards stand behind them. No text. The upper-left sky and foliage above Ramayyan hold both balloons without touching faces.

Varma, on the left, has a loose curly mane falling to his neck instead of a knot above his LEFT ear. His fuller, rounder face reads as Nagoji's sheet, not varma-v1, and it is inconsistent with panels 2 and 4 on the same page. Next to the real Nagoji, both men wear gold-bordered cream cloths and look alike. Nagoji's brand is drawn as a pink-purple round blot at the top of the white scar. It reads as a fresh wound or bruise on an 'uninjured' man, not a pale puckered scar patch. The rest works: Ramayyan is mid-bow in the middle with his head turned toward Nagoji, Nagoji has his high topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud, moustache, clean chin and silver chain, and the guards are settled with their torches.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Varma on the left, Ramayyan mid-bow in the centre with his head tilted toward Nagoji, and Nagoji waiting at the right edge of the torchlight, with the guards and their torches settled at the foot of the lit stair. Fix Varma so he matches panels 2 and 4 and never resembles Nagoji. Take his face from the varma-v1 sheet's profile study: a long, lean face with high cheekbones, a long straight nose and deep-set eyes. Comb his black hair smooth and tie it in one compact knot above and behind his LEFT ear, with no loose curls hanging to the neck or shoulders. Keep the white pearl drop earrings, one gold chain, a thin line of sandal paste across the brow and a cream mundu with a thin gold border, and have him turned toward Ramayyan. Give Nagoji a PLAIN cream shoulder cloth with no wide gold border so the two men read apart at a glance. His old brand is only a pale, flesh-toned, puckered patch of raised scar ridges on the INNER left forearm beside the long thin white scar, with no red, pink or purple colour, so it never looks like a fresh wound. Or turn the forearm inward so only the white scar edge shows. Keep the open dusk sky at the upper right and the foliage band across the top clear for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor: Varma's hair is mostly loose curls, with only a loosely gathered mass above his LEFT ear standing in for the side knot. He wears a vertical white namam where the script asks for a horizontal sandal line. Over-the-shoulder framing, Nagoji's topknot, grey temples, flush gold stud and silver chain, the pearl drops and single gold chain, and the dusk torchlit stair setting all match. The two balloons fit in the sky and canopy at upper centre, between the two heads.

Minor: this is a medium close-up, chest up, not a tight face close-up. Otherwise it is clean: thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, high topknot, tiny flush stud, no forehead mark, and a wry, almost-smile expression. The caption fits in the clear dusk sky at upper left.

Minor: a torch is mounted on a post at frame left, where the setting asks for no posts. Varma's knot sits at the back of his crown and is not clearly above the LEFT ear, which is turned away from camera. Varma and the heir carry namam marks rather than a sandal line. The beat reads well: Varma climbs ahead looking up at the bare rock, the heir is at his side, and Nagoji follows behind, unarmed, with the scar showing on his inner left forearm. The balloon fits over the night sky and grey rock face at upper centre.

Minor: Varma's hair is a topknot on the crown, not a side knot (this matches page 1 panels 1.2 and 1.4). Varma and the heir stand beside the jackfruit tree rather than directly under it, and they face camera rather than the sanctum; the boy's eyes do turn up-left toward it. The lingam inside is clearer than 'faintly'. Every other script element is present: the jasmine-hung sanctum, lamp niches in the peeling lime-wash, the roots heaving the flags, the cropped-hair assistant with a torch and a basket of ghee pots, and the sleeping dog. The long caption fits over the plain foreground stone at bottom left, or over the stone floor at bottom centre-right.

Minor: Varma's face is a little rounder and younger than the varma-v1 sheet. He wears a vertical namam rather than a sandal line. This is the best match of the page for the side knot: it sits above his LEFT ear with a pearl drop below. His hand rests soundly on the heir's shoulder as he turns toward off-panel right with a sly half-smile. The boy keeps his palms pressed, with eyes wide toward the doorway. The marks on the lingam are three ash stripes, not pseudo-text. The long balloon fits over the night sky and mandapa roofline at upper centre, or the plain lime-washed wall below it.

v01 has strong staging: Nagoji sits on the jackfruit roots at screen right with his eyes sliding sideways, and Varma and the heir stoop at the jasmine-hung sanctum doorway while the old priest lights lamps before the ash-marked lingam. Nagoji's thick moustache, clean chin (light shading only), flush gold stud and silver chain are correct. The blocking problem is Varma: his hair has obvious silver-grey streaks through the temple and side. That breaks the MUST MATCH line ('black hair, never the grey of the sheet's older figure') and his pure black hair in 2.4 and 4.1. His knot also sits at the back of his head, not above the LEFT ear. Smaller problems: Nagoji's brand is drawn as a crisp dark circular star symbol that reads as a tattoo, not a blurred burn, and he has an extra long scar on his upper arm as well as the forearm scar.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, lighting and setting exactly: Nagoji seated on the jackfruit roots at screen right, three-quarter to us, his eyes sliding sideways away from the sanctum; at screen left Varma and the heir stooping at the low jasmine-hung sanctum doorway, the elderly old priest inside lighting the lamps before the ash-marked black lingam. Fix Varma's hair: it must be solid jet-black with NO grey, silver or white strands anywhere, tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear, the same black hair he has in the neighbouring panels. Only the old priest has grey hair. On Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, draw the old Goa brand as a pale, puckered, raised burn patch blurred past reading (not a dark tattoo, circle, star or symbol). Beside it draw ONE long thin white scar running toward the elbow, and no other scar on his upper arm. Keep the dark night sky and leaves across the top middle of the frame low in detail for two captions.

decisions.issues: v01 has the four requested insets along the bottom: bangled wrist on the outer steps, temple assistant with torch, old priest's hands with wicks, sleeping dog. But it adds a large establishing scene above them that the script does not call for, and that scene breaks continuity. The old priest sits cross-legged out in the courtyard with a full white beard, a rudraksha mala and a red-bordered cloth. In 3.1 he is clean-shaven, in a gold-bordered cloth, inside the sanctum lighting lamps, and his sheet face is clean-shaven. The sanctum is also empty, though Varma and the heir should be at its doorway. In the inset, the temple assistant wears a red-bordered shoulder cloth; his figure tag and 2.4 say no shoulder cloth.
decisions.correction: Draw ONLY the four small insets, four equal panels in a single row or a 2x2 grid that fills the whole frame, separated by thin gutters, with NO larger establishing scene above or around them: 1) a woman's bangled wrist and the hem of her cloth disappearing down the outer stone steps into the dark; 2) the temple assistant, a bare-chested youth of about seventeen with close-cropped hair, a plain cream mundu and NO shoulder cloth, no ash on his brow, waiting by a mandapa pillar holding his torch; 3) only the old priest's hands, inside the lamplit sanctum, pressing a wick into ghee in a small brass lamp, his cream mundu with a thin gold border at the edge of the frame (no red border, no rudraksha beads, no face shown); 4) the brown-and-white courtyard dog asleep on the stone flags, one front paw twitching. Night, warm niche-lamp and torchlight as before. Leave plain dark shadow in the upper part of the first inset for one short caption.

decisions.issues: The chaver is well drawn: young, lean, clean-shaven, ordinary face, three ash stripes, knot at the nape, cloth over his LEFT shoulder, sacred thread, brass plate with flowers and a clay lamp, stepping out of the side-room door. Two problems. First, a dark sheath and hilt with brass fittings hangs at his hip outside the cloth. That spoils the beat 'every detail of him is correct' and contradicts 4.2, where the dagger comes from beneath his cloth. Second, the sanctum doorway is fully in frame at left and empty. The script has him gazing at the boy at the sanctum OUT of frame, and in 3.1 Varma, the heir and the old priest are all at that doorway.
decisions.correction: Keep the chaver exactly as drawn: young, lean and wiry, clean-shaven with an ordinary face, three thick ash stripes on the forehead, oiled hair in a tight knot low at the nape, white cloth at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder, sacred thread, both hands holding the small brass plate with flowers and a clay lamp, stepping barefoot out of the lit side-room doorway by the peeling lime-washed wall, with the jackfruit roots at screen right. Remove everything at his waist: no dagger, knife, hilt, sheath, cord or dark object at his hip or tucked into his cloth. His waist cloth is plain and smooth, and the blade stays completely hidden. Frame the shot so the sanctum doorway is NOT in view. The left side of the frame shows only the lime-washed wall with niche lamps and the edge of a mandapa pillar, and his gaze runs off the left edge of the frame toward the unseen boy. Keep the night sky above the wall clear for one short caption.

decisions.issues: v01 shows the empty courtyard: sanctum, lime-washed wall, jackfruit tree, and no figure at all. The script beat is an extreme letterbox close-up of the chaver's eyes and the three ash stripes, lit from below by the clay lamp. The panel misses the beat entirely.
decisions.correction: This panel is an extreme close-up, NOT a view of the courtyard, with no architecture and no other figure. Fill the wide 3-to-1 strip edge to edge with the chaver's face, cropped from just above the three thick horizontal white ash stripes on his forehead down to the bridge of his nose. Both eyes are wide open, unblinking and perfectly still, fixed on something just off the left edge. He is a young, ordinary-looking man, clean-shaven, with oiled black hair pulled back from the brow. Light his face warmly from below by the small clay-lamp flame, with deep shadow above the stripes and at the temples. Keep both eyes and the stripes in the middle half of the strip's height and width. Leave plain dark shadow at the far left and far right ends of the strip for two captions, clear of the eyes.

decisions.issues: Screen direction, setting and lighting are right. The chaver is on the left walking left, eyes down, cloth over his LEFT shoulder; niche-lamp flames bend while the plate flame burns straight up. Nagoji under the tree on the right is on model: high topknot, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain. But the chaver carries a large, clearly visible sheathed dagger tucked at his waist. That contradicts the hidden blade, which only appears from beneath his cloth in 4.2, and the beat that every detail of him looks correct. The two men are also half a frame apart, not within arm's length.
decisions.correction: Keep the setting, night lamplight, both costumes and the screen direction: the chaver on the LEFT walking left toward the sanctum, brass plate in both hands, eyes down and not looking at Nagoji; Nagoji on the RIGHT under the jackfruit tree, high topknot, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, silver chain, unarmed. Remove the dagger entirely: no hilt, sheath, knife or dark object at the chaver's waist or anywhere in the picture. His waist cloth is smooth and plain. Bring the two men within arm's length: the chaver passes directly in front of Nagoji, only a single step between them, with Nagoji's head turned toward him, lips slightly parted as he speaks softly. Keep the niche-lamp flames bending and the plate flame straight up. Leave the dark sky and the upper tree trunk above their heads clear for a speech balloon near Nagoji and a short caption.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the chaver's mouth is nearly closed rather than visibly speaking; Varma and the boy wear a vertical namam rather than a horizontal line of sandal paste; the lamp on the plate is brass rather than clay; the boy stands mid-courtyard rather than right at the sanctum threshold. Faces, costume, three-figure count, setting (jasmine sanctum left, peeling lime-wash wall with niche lamps, jackfruit tree right) and the dark upper sky/wall for the balloon and two captions are all sound.

Acceptable with small deviations: the chaver shows light stubble along the jaw (script says clean-shaven), bushier hair than in 4.1, and no ash stripes on his arm; the dagger is held reverse-grip at his hip pointing down rather than laid back along the forearm; Nagoji wears a plain silver bangle on his right wrist and carries the same heavy grey at the temples as on page 3. The beat is clear: plate, flowers and clay lamp falling, dagger in the chaver's left hand, Varma (black hair, side knot, pearl earrings, one gold chain, no crest or spear) planted with arms wide, the heir behind him, Nagoji launching by the tree. No painted text.

The chaver wears a dark brown sleeveless tunic and a red head-wrap, a different costume from his white temple cloth in 3.3 to 4.2. Varma's hair is grey at the temples and sides, which breaks the bible rule of black hair with no grey. The dagger blade is fully visible in the foreground, but the script says the assistant's body hides the blade entirely. Varma stands passively in the background instead of beside the lunge line. The assistant comes in from the tree side (right), not from the mandapa side (left).
decisions.correction: The chaver must be the same young, lean, clean-shaven temple man as in the previous panels: bare-chested with a sacred thread, a plain white cloth wrapped at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder, oiled black hair in a tight knot low at the nape, three horizontal ash stripes on the brow; NO dark tunic or vest, NO red head-wrap or sash. Seen from just behind his right shoulder in the foreground, his low lunge drives into the picture past Varma's bare shoulder: Varma close in the mid-ground just right of centre, braced square with arms still wide, the heir hidden behind him and out of frame. Varma's hair is fully BLACK with no grey at the temples or sides, in a side knot above his LEFT ear, with pearl drop earrings and one gold chain. The bare-chested temple assistant hurls himself in from screen LEFT (the mandapa and sanctum side) across the line between the chaver and Varma, so that his torso completely covers the chaver's hand and blade: no steel visible anywhere in the frame. Keep the night courtyard, the jasmine-hung sanctum at left, the jackfruit tree at right, the assistant's close-cropped hair, open mouth and raised burning torch, and keep the dark sky at the top clear for one short balloon.

decisions.issues: The generator painted the inset as a small bordered box in the upper-left corner of an otherwise empty wide courtyard. That is a painted panel border, and the actual beat (the assistant's silhouetted fall with the torch rolling) fills less than a fifth of the frame. Placed as the 4.4 inset, the frame would show an empty courtyard.
decisions.correction: Draw this as one single full-frame image with no inset box, no frame within the frame, no border line and no wider empty courtyard around it. The whole picture, seen low at floor level, is the dark silhouette of the bare-chested, close-cropped temple assistant crumpling onto the worn stone flags, knees buckling and one arm folding under him, backlit by niche-lamp glow. His torch has fallen from his hand and rolls across the flags in the foreground, its flame spilling a streak of orange light over the stones. Show the fall only: no wound, no blood, no dagger, no other figure. Keep the night palette, the wet-looking worn flags and a hint of a pillar base and a niche lamp behind him.

decisions.issues: Nagoji clamps the dagger wrist with his RIGHT arm, which comes from his right shoulder with his chest facing the viewer, and the brand and long scar are painted on that right forearm. The script and the injury continuity need his LEFT hand on the wrist (that palm is cut at 5.4), with the brand only on the inner LEFT forearm. The chaver wears a brown sleeveless vest and a maroon sash with loose curly hair, unlike the white-clad, nape-knotted temple man of 3.3 to 4.2. Nagoji's face, topknot, grey temple streak, gold stud and silver chain, the dog and the setting are good.
decisions.correction: Nagoji must clamp the chaver's dagger wrist with his LEFT hand. Stage the chaver on the left lunging toward screen left, toward the sanctum, his body turned partly to the viewer with the dagger in his LEFT hand nearest the viewer. Draw Nagoji crashing in from the right edge, seen from his left side, so the arm nearest the viewer is his LEFT arm, shooting forward from his LEFT shoulder to lock his left hand around the chaver's LEFT wrist, while his LEFT shoulder drives into the chaver's ribs and his right arm stays back behind his body. The pale puckered brand and the long white scar appear only on that LEFT inner forearm, never on his right arm. The chaver must look exactly as in the previous panels: young, lean, clean-shaven with no stubble, three horizontal ash stripes on the brow, oiled black hair in a tight knot low at the nape, bare-chested with a sacred thread, a plain white cloth wrapped at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder. NO brown vest or tunic, NO maroon sash. Keep the night courtyard with the jasmine-hung sanctum at left and the jackfruit tree at right, Nagoji's face, high topknot, grey temple streak, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, the dog bolting and barking in the background, and the dark sky at the top clear for a short caption.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): setting, lighting, Varma (bare chest, one gold chain, pearl drop earring, cream mundu, no spear) and the heir all match. The priest is wrong, though. He is a black-haired man of about thirty-five. In panel 3.1 and the MUST MATCH line he is the grey-haired old priest at the sanctum lamps, so readers would take this man for a second, unknown person. He also does not catch or haul the boy: he peers from behind a pillar at the right edge with his arms folded across his chest, and the boy's hand never reaches him. That pillar is on the struggle and tree side, so the boy is being sent toward the fight instead of back toward the sanctum. Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown, not above his LEFT ear.
decisions.correction: Fix the old priest and the direction of the shove; keep everything else that worked (the night courtyard, sanctum doorway with jasmine and faint lingam at screen LEFT, peeling lime-washed wall with niche lamps, jackfruit tree at screen RIGHT, Varma's bare chest, one thin gold chain, pearl drop earring and cream gold-bordered mundu, the heir's look and wide staring eyes, clear wall and sky in the upper middle for the captions). The old priest must be visibly ELDERLY and the same man seen lighting the sanctum lamps earlier: grey-white hair tied in a knot, a lined, thin face from the temple priest sheet aged by thirty years, a slight stoop, white shoulder cloth with a gold border. He stands at a stone mandapa pillar at screen LEFT, on the sanctum side, with BOTH arms reaching out and actually gripping the boy, pulling him in behind that pillar. Varma is at centre-right, his body half turned toward the struggle off panel to the RIGHT, one arm swung back so his hand on the boy's shoulder shoves the boy LEFTWARD to the priest. His black hair is in a side knot above his LEFT ear. The boy stumbles leftward into the priest's hands, head twisted back over his shoulder, still staring right toward the unseen fight. No other figures; nobody stands between the boy and the right edge.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Nagoji is on the right and matches his sheet and bible row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, high topknot with grey at the temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth. His LEFT hand is locked on the chaver's dagger wrist with the dagger trembling between them. The chaver on the left is clean-shaven, with ash stripes, sweat and bared teeth. There is no painted text and no blood. Minor: the chaver's costume and hair do not follow the script (ochre torn sleeveless top, red sash and loose long curls, instead of white cloth over the left shoulder, a sacred thread and a knot at the nape). This does match his brown top and red sash in 4.3 and 4.5. The brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm is a small dark round stamp-like mark next to the white scar, not a pale puckered patch, but it has no readable letters. Caption space: the sky and wall top along the upper band, plus the leaves at upper right or the floor and roots at lower right.

v01 (the only candidate): Nagoji's look is right (moustache, clean chin, gold stud, topknot with grey temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth), and the chaver's elbow into his ribs reads well. But there are two daggers. The chaver holds a curved dagger free in his near hand at his waist, while Nagoji's left hand grips a different wrist at the bottom centre: a second fist holding a second hilt with a gold pommel. The real blade is therefore uncontrolled, which breaks the beat ('his left hand still on the wrist'), and the chapter's single-dagger rule. The chaver has also lost his ash stripes. The brand on Nagoji's forearm is a dark omega-like glyph that could read as a letter.
decisions.correction: Exactly ONE dagger and exactly four hands in the picture. The chaver (on the LEFT) holds his single dagger in his RIGHT hand, the hand nearer the viewer, and Nagoji's LEFT hand is clamped around THAT same right wrist, pinning the blade low and pointing away from both bodies. Draw no second hilt, second knife or extra fist anywhere, and nothing in Nagoji's right hand. The chaver's LEFT arm is the one bent sharply, its elbow slamming into Nagoji's ribs under the chest; that left hand is empty. Nagoji (on the RIGHT) folds around the blow, grimacing, his right arm close to his side. Keep the chaver clean-shaven with no moustache and give him back his three thick white horizontal ash stripes across the forehead. Draw the brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm only as a pale, puckered patch of raised scar ridges beside the long white scar: no dark ink, no symbol and no letter-like shape. Keep everything else: the night courtyard with the sanctum and jasmine at screen left and the jackfruit tree at screen right, the niche lamps, Nagoji's topknot with grey temples, gold stud, silver chain and cream mundu with gold-bordered shoulder cloth, the chaver's ochre sleeveless top and dark red sash, and the clear night sky and wall in the upper part for the caption.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): wrong cast. The attacker holding the dagger on the left has Nagoji's captivity look: thick moustache, gold ear stud, long loose curls, torn ochre tunic and bandaged wrists. He is not a clean-shaven chaver. The figure on the right, with a pearl drop earring and a gold bead necklace, is Varma, and he is the one gripping the attacker's wrist. Ananthan Pillai (topknot with grey temples, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth) is missing entirely, so Nagoji's LEFT hand dragging on the chaver's wrist is not shown. The panel reads as Nagoji attacking the king. It also breaks screen direction: Varma should come in from the left (6.1, 6.3) with Nagoji on the right.
decisions.correction: Draw exactly THREE men, with no doubles. LEFT: Marthanda Varma, with the face, moustache and heavier build from his sheet, black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, ONE thin gold chain, bare chest, cream mundu with a thin gold border, no turban, no crest, no spear. He steps IN toward the blade, weight driving forward, front foot advancing, hands rising, calm and set; he does not lean back. CENTRE: the chaver, a young, lean, wiry stranger, CLEAN-SHAVEN with NO moustache, NO ear ornament and NO wrist bandages, three thick white horizontal ash stripes across his forehead, short dark curly hair, in the same ochre sleeveless top, dark red sash and white lower cloth as the previous panels. He thrusts his single dagger upward, its point aimed at Varma's throat a hand-span short of it, never touching it. RIGHT: Nagoji as Ananthan Pillai: high Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu with a gold-bordered shoulder cloth, bare arms, no bandages, never the torn ochre captivity tunic. His LEFT hand is locked on the chaver's dagger wrist, dragging it back toward the right. The dagger is the only blade, and there is no blood. Keep the night courtyard with the sanctum and jasmine at screen left, the niche lamps on the peeling lime-washed wall, the jackfruit tree at screen right and the warm lamplight.

decisions.issues: v01 is the wrong beat and has no chaver at all. Only two men are drawn. Varma holds the dagger himself and drives his hand into NAGOJI's throat, while Nagoji grips Varma's wrist, so it reads as the king attacking Nagoji. Varma's hair is a bun on the crown, not a side knot above his LEFT ear. The courtyard, lamps, tree and Nagoji's look (moustache, grey temples, silver chain, stud) are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: Draw THREE men, not two. The chaver, the assassin, stands in the CENTRE and holds the only dagger. He is young, lean and wiry, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, with three thick horizontal white ash stripes across his forehead and oiled black hair tied in a tight knot low at the nape. He wears white cloth at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder, plus a thin sacred thread. His dagger arm thrusts up toward Varma. Varma is at screen LEFT, inside the dagger's arc: face from the varma sheet, black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, pearl drop earrings, one gold chain, bare chest, cream mundu with a thin gold border, and no weapon. His left hand clamps the CHAVER's forearm. His right hand drives stiff-fingered into the CHAVER's throat in a kalari strike, with a calm, practised face. Varma never holds the dagger and never touches Nagoji. Nagoji is at the right edge: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, high topknot, grey temples, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth. His LEFT hand stays locked on the chaver's dagger wrist just below Varma's grip, and he is not being struck. Keep this version's courtyard, niche lamps, sanctum at left, jackfruit tree at right and the open dark sky in the upper centre for one long caption.

decisions.issues: The head-butt beat and Varma's reel are well staged, but the chaver is drawn with a fully SHAVED head and a rudraksha mala, with no sacred thread and no shoulder cloth. Next to the curly-haired, nape-knotted chaver of 6.4 and 6.5 he reads as a different man. Varma's forehead mark is a set of vertical namam lines, not the horizontal sandal-paste line, and it is not shown smeared or broken. His hair knot sits at the back of the head rather than above his left ear.
decisions.correction: The chaver must keep his hair: oiled curly black hair tied back in a tight knot low at the nape, never a shaved or bald head. He is young, lean and wiry, CLEAN-SHAVEN with no moustache, with three thick horizontal white ash stripes across his forehead. He wears a thin white sacred thread across the chest (no rudraksha beads) and white cloth at the waist and over his LEFT shoulder. Varma's forehead mark is a single HORIZONTAL line of pale sandal paste across the brow, visibly smeared and broken by the impact, never vertical namam lines. His black hair is in a side knot above his LEFT ear, with pearl drop earrings and one gold chain.
